acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc: Ira goes out with a letter carrier, ‘Grace,’ as she delivers mail on her route. He learns about the people who bring us our mail and also how people treat their mail.

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc:
Writing a letter decades after an event that shaped her life was the only way that Nicole Piasecki could make some sense of it.
A version of this essay first appeared in Hippocampus Magazine.
acts.credits: By Nicole Piasecki; Produced by Chris Benderev
acts.title: Dear Alice

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc:
Yorkshire, 1866. A farmer overcomes his timidity and writes a very important letter to a local beauty.
This letter was performed by Taron Egerton at Union Chapel, London, for Letters Live, which stages live readings of famous and remarkable letters in front of an audience.
acts.title: Dear Miss

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: When senior editor David Kestenbaum was still a rookie reporter, he wrote an email to a legend. Then he waited...and waited...for a reply.
acts.title: Dear Dr. Kestenbaum

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc:
A woman writes an unusual letter on behalf of her husband.
This letter was performed by Crystal Clarke at the Royal Albert Hall, London, for Letters Live.
acts.title: Dear US Army

acts.label: Act Five
acts.desc: Producer Zoe Chace compares the letters a person gets and the letters they wish they got.
acts.credits: By Zoe Chace; Produced by Nancy Updike

songs.a: The Presidents of the United States of America

acts.title: Dear Zoe
